fixes.explanation: David never mentions being sick in this psalm. He says he's distraught "…at the voice of the enemy, at the pressure of the wicked." So the trouble is coming from people, not from his body. Nobody here is reaching for a thermometer and telling him to rest.

David says, "In the wilderness I would remain." Not just a quick visit either, he says he would stay. Far from the noise is where he pictures rest. Then comes "Selah," and I'll let you sit with that picture a moment.
No palace in this dream. David says, "In the wilderness I would remain." He pictures staying far away, out where the wilderness is. That's the escape he's wishing for.

The psalm never says that about them here. David asks the Lord to confuse their speech "…for I see violence and strife in the city." Violence and strife are what he's looking at, so that's what he prays about. I think when the city looks like that, other gods aren't the first thing on his mind.

Right, the inside is no safer. David says, "Day and night they encircle the walls, while malice and trouble lie within." He adds, "Destruction is within…" and "oppression and deceit never leave the streets." So the trouble circles the walls, and it's inside too.

David says, "We shared sweet fellowship together; we walked with the crowd into the house of God." So they walked into the house of God together, with the crowd. That's a lot of shared road behind them. I think that's why the turn hurts so much.

The psalm never says David gathers anybody. He says, "But I call to God, and the LORD saves me." Nobody gets a roll call, he just calls on God. I bet that's one phone call that never goes to voicemail, but that's me talking, not the psalm.
David says the opposite. He says, "Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice." The verse says God hears him. Nothing in it says God gets tired of hearing him.

Right. David says, "Morning, noon, and night, I cry out in distress, and He hears my voice." He cries out morning, noon and night, and he says God hears his voice. Nothing there says God gets tired of it.

Offerings aren't mentioned in this part of the psalm. David says it's "…because they do not change and they have no fear of God." That's the reason the text gives, and it's about who they are, not what they skipped bringing. I'd have loved to hand out a checklist, but the psalm doesn't have one.

The priests aren't named in this verse. David says, "Cast your burden upon the LORD and He will sustain you…" The burden goes straight to the LORD, with no middleman. Think of it like a heavy box of cookies, and he's saying hand it to the One who can hold it.
